Two fixes for Windows. Install this over v0.1.1: your library, videos and
settings are kept.

## Downloads

| | file | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows 10 / 11** | `Voxframe-0.1.2-Windows-setup.exe` | Not code-signed: Windows SmartScreen will ask you to confirm. [How to install](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/install-windows.md) |
| **macOS (Apple Silicon) — early** | `Voxframe-0.1.2-macOS-arm64.dmg` | **Early build.** Unsigned, so macOS will ask you to confirm in System Settings. Apple Silicon Macs only. [How to open it](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/install-mac.md) |

Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`, attached below.

Both downloads include FFmpeg 9.0.2, which is licensed under the GPL, as a
separate program. Its complete source is attached to this release
(`ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz`, with FFmpeg's signature `ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.asc`), with
`ffmpeg-9.0.2-libraries.txt`: the libraries compiled into each build and where
their source is published.

## Fixed

- **Long videos failed at the very end** on Windows with *"The filename or
  extension is too long"*. A video with more than about 120 scenes joined all
  its pieces in one step, whose instructions grew past a limit Windows sets.
  The pieces are now joined in smaller groups, with every crossfade kept.
- **Installing over a running Voxframe** could leave it half-updated. The
  installer and the uninstaller now check first, and ask you to click **Quit**
  in Voxframe's small window before they carry on.

## Privacy

Your recordings and videos stay on your computer. See
[the privacy note](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/privacy.md).
